subject: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@finpay.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@finpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up & next steps

Hi Carlos / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we can align the integration plan: 

Summary of requirements we captured
- Private connectivity: you prefer to avoid public internet egress from your model/control-plane traffic (AWS environment). Considering AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint) or an IP allowlist + egress controls.
- Auth: preference for mTLS for control plane access; SDKs should support short-lived tokens for user-level calls.
- Networking: IP allowlists, egress restrictions, DNS override for internal resolution to Redwood endpoints, and support for mutual TLS termination.
- Integration: SDK setup (Python/Go), structured output/tool-calling for downstream systems, embeddings + reranker pipeline (we’ll provide embedding endpoints; you’ll host vectors in your VPC or we can support encrypted storage).
- Compliance: your security team wants audit logs and confirmation on data egress and update channels.

What Redwood can do (high-level)
- Support PrivateLink / VPC endpoints for Private deployments and Dedicated customers; we also support IP allowlisting and mTLS.
- SDKs work with either API tokens or mTLS; we recommend mTLS for the highest assurance environment.
- We can provide a private hosted DNS entry (private hosted zone) so endpoints resolve to your VPC endpoints.
- Embeddings: we support encrypted-at-rest storage; can offer a reranker pipeline that runs inside the private network or via secure peering depending on your compliance needs.

Open questions from our side
- Do you have a network diagram we can review (NAT, egress gateways, firewall rules, and whether you want passthrough TLS or LB termination)?
- Which model for private connectivity do you prefer initially (PrivateLink vs. IP allowlist)?
- Any constraints on scheduled ports or CIDR blocks we should be aware of?

Proposed next steps
1) Please share a current network diagram and firewall rules (attachment will be helpful). Jonas will review and propose the specific allowlist/CIDR needs.
2) Technical deep-dive with our SEs (Jonas + Marissa) — proposed: Wed 5/12 @ 10:00 AM PT (open to moving earlier).
3) Jonas to draft the networking checklist; Marissa to prepare an SDK/auth guide and sample mTLS config.
4) Lauren to create a mutual action plan (MAP) and circulate with dates and owners.

Thanks — if 5/12 10am PT doesn't work, propose another time and we’ll accommodate.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up & next steps

Hi Carlos / Priya — thanks for the attachments, that helps. Quick technical clarifications / answers below (happy to expand on the call):

1) PrivateLink / VPC endpoints: yes — for Redwood Private (and Dedicated in many regions) we support AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints). That route keeps control-plane traffic inside AWS and avoids public internet egress for API calls.

2) mTLS and auth: we support both mTLS and short-lived tokens. Recommended pattern for highest assurance: mTLS for the control plane (mutual TLS between your infrastructure and our endpoint) + short-lived tokens for user/session-level SDK auth. We can provide guidance for automated client cert rotation (ACM or your existing PKI).

3) Model updates / package downloads: model artifact pulls can be configured to happen over the PrivateLink endpoint in most setups. If you prefer, we can stage artifacts into a customer-controlled S3 bucket via secure replicate so no public egress is required.

4) DNS: we can publish a private hosted zone that resolves to the PrivateLink ENIs. Alternately, you can create resolver rules pointing to our hosted zone. Either approach works — we’ll provide step-by-step.

5) IP allowlist / CIDRs: I’ll draft an expected set of conservative CIDRs (we often provide a small set per region) and a recommended firewall policy. I do need to know whether you will terminate TLS at a load balancer (and pass through mTLS) or if you plan to have mTLS peer-to-peer to Redwood's endpoints. Please confirm.

6) Embeddings / reranker: we support running the reranker inside your VPC for fully private execution, or we can host encrypted storage with strict access controls. If you need vectors to remain in your VPC, we’ll provide a connector pattern that avoids moving vectors offsite.

I’ve attached a short draft of a networking checklist (draft_mmp.docx) and will refine it after the call.

Can we lock Wed 5/12 at 9:00 AM PT for the deep-dive? If that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite and include an agenda: networking diagram walkthrough, allowlist/CIDR confirmation, SDK auth flow, and embeddings options.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
